- [USER] User expressed interest in unique cultural practices and festivals in India.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Holi is a festival of colors celebrated all over India, symbolizing diversity, love, and inclusivity, with roots in Hindu mythology celebrating the victory of good over evil.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Durga Puja is celebrated in West Bengal, Assam, and other parts of Eastern India, marking the victory of good over evil and reflecting the region’s devotion to the goddess Durga.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Diwali is the festival of lights celebrated all over India, marked by lighting earthen lamps, candles, and fireworks, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Onam is a harvest festival celebrated in Kerala, marked by grand feasts, traditional dances, and boat races, paying homage to the king believed to have ruled during Kerala's golden era.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bihu is celebrated in Assam three times a year (Rongali Bihu, Bhogali Bihu, and Kangali Bihu), marking the onset of spring and reflecting the region’s agricultural practices.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Navratri is a nine-day festival celebrated all over India, marking the nine forms of the Hindu goddess Durga, celebrated with traditional dances, music, and devotional songs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Rath Yatra is an annual festival in Odisha celebrating the Hindu god Jagannath, commemorating his journey from his temple to his aunt's temple, reflecting the state’s cultural heritage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] These festivals reflect India's religious and cultural diversity and are a testament to the country's rich cultural heritage and community harmony.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Diwali is generally considered the most popular festival in India, celebrated by people of all religions and regions, marked by lighting lamps and fireworks, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.
